m0001.summary: At the start of the King's state visit, Lima repeats his congratulations on the welcome in Madrid; coded: all continues without news, he is writing to Windsor.
m0001.en:
I again congratulate Your Majesty on the warm welcome received there, which has made the happiest impression among
us. Everything continues without news. I am writing to Windsor. I kiss Your Majesty's hands. Wenceslau de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. Only "Tudo continua sem novidade. Escrevo Windsor" is coded (four groups); the rest is in clear on the form. The King
was in Madrid on the first leg of his state visit of November 1909 (Madrid, Paris, London); Windsor is a later stop.
The first figure of 05764 and the fourth of 80054 are not sure; the glosses are clear.

m0005.summary: Confidential: a stop at Bussaco would be awkward, so the King should come straight by the night express; Vasconcellos Porto presses for an answer.
m0005.en:
Confidential. A stop at Bussaco would have been awkward, so I insist on the advantage of coming straight through,
leaving there [Paris] by the night express. Vasconcellos Porto is pressing for the answer, which I earnestly ask of Your
Majesty. I kiss Your Majesty's hands. Wenceslau de [Lima].

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. "teve" (had) is the gloss; the sense is conditional. Vasconcellos Porto is presumably the minister in charge of the
King's return journey [our identification, not checked].

m0007.summary: The return journey settled: arrival in Lisbon at 1.15 pm, greetings at Vilar Formoso, rest as far as Pampilhosa, lunch between Santarém and Lisbon.
m0007.en:
I thank Your Majesty for your telegram and for agreeing to the proposals. Arrival time in Lisbon a quarter past one
in the afternoon. Any earlier would be awkward, because the train would pass Pampilhosa and Coimbra too early; any
later would make the journey needlessly slow. I should be most grateful if Your Majesty would tell me whether you will
receive greetings on entering Portugal at Vilar Formoso, where they very much wish to offer them. After that there
will be none, because it will be night, so that you can rest as far as Pampilhosa, which you reach at 8 in the
morning. Lunch between Santarém and Lisbon, from half past [?] to a quarter past one. I kiss Your Majesty's hands.
Wenceslau de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. Mostly in clear. 50667 is circled on the form;

m0009.summary: No answer yet to Saturday's telegram about the return trains; the departure is the day after tomorrow and nothing is fixed; Lima asks for a decision most urgently.
m0009.en:
The lack of an answer to Saturday's telegram about the return trains is causing the greatest trouble. I remind you
that the day after tomorrow is the day of Your Majesty's departure, and nothing is fixed for want of that instruction,
which I ask for most urgently. Vasconcellos Porto has telegraphed [two groups unread]. [We are working] on the
assumption of the Northern express, but Your Majesty's decision is missing. I kiss Your Majesty's hands. Wenceslau de
Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. "Saturday's telegram" is m0011 of 27 Nov 1909, a Saturday. The glosses over 18703 and 10586 are too faint to read
("comp..são", "Th.." [?]). The office noted that a correction would follow for a missing word; the word count is one
short.

m0011.summary: Lima proposes the return route: the 7.40 pm night train from Paris to Medina del Campo and a special train to Lisbon, cutting out the stop at Luso.
m0011.en:
In agreement [?] with Porto and Serpa we settled that the best course would be to take there [in Paris] the [?] night
[train] at 7.40 pm, in full comfort, as well as or better than the Sud-Express, and come as far as Medina [del Campo],
where a special train would wait that would reach Lisbon at 11 in the morning, or later if preferred. This would cut
out the stop on the way at Luso, which is awkward and makes a bad impression. The service is better arranged in the
way I indicate. [...] comfortable at Hen[daye?] [...] already at 8-something, and at Medina for the special train at
about 7 in the evening. Awaiting [the orders of] Your Majesty, so as to give the orders, which are urgent. W. de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. The first pass read the margin gloss as "Em Coimbra";

m0014.summary: Since the French President has given the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour to Bocage, the King should be friendly to Briand, with no inequality against England and Spain.
m0014.en:
I remind Your Majesty that, since the President of the Republic has given the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour to
Bocage, it matters to be friendly to Briand and leave no bad impression; above all there must be no inequality with
what was done in England and Spain. I kiss Your Majesty's hands. Wenceslau de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. Bocage is presumably Carlos du Bocage, Portuguese foreign minister in 1909, and Briand the French premier [our
identifications, not checked]. The point is a Portuguese decoration for Briand in return. 93186 is glossed
"G.C. Legião" (the first pass had "a decoration, gloss unclear").

m0018.summary: Lima edits the King's reply toast for the President's dinner, adding friendship, thanks for the welcome in "intellectual Paris" and the tightening of relations.
m0018.en:
Since our welcome in France has been so affectionate, it seems right to make the [dinner?] toast warmer. In the first
section, after "sympathy", add "and friendship"; in the second, after "you have done", say "for the welcome the French
nation gives us in its great and beautiful capital, its intellectual Paris". In the third section, after "between
Portugal and France", insert "and also for the closer tightening of their relations". If the President of the
Republic's toast contains anything special, make the due allusion in the reply, [?] discreet and prudent. I kiss Your
Majesty's hands. Wenceslau de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. The minister edits the King's reply toast for the dinner given by the President of the Republic. 69958 and 66931 are
glossed "tend" and "es":

m0020.summary: Confidential: the King should go only to São Carlos on the night of his arrival and hold the reception at the station; Lima asks for an answer.
m0020.en:
Confidential. It seems best that Your Majesty go only to [the theatre of] São Carlos on the night of the day of
arrival. [Someone] told me whether [...] I can count on that [the clause is not clear]. It also seems better that Your
Majesty hold the reception at the station, where a suitably prepared room will be ready. That will make the reception
easier and better and will free the arrival arrangements in the preparation. I await Your Majesty's decision. I
earnestly ask Your Majesty for an answer, because the arrangements have to be ordered. I kiss Your Majesty's hands.
Wenceslau de Lima.

Notes. From the pencil decode of the time above the groups; in the reading [ ] marks our addition and [?] a group not read or doubtful. Line 2 is read with the corrected glosses: 51443 "contar com", 19864 "isso" (as in line 3), 05068 "inconveniencia"
[?], 19313 "posso" or "pouco" [?].
